messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: N/A
Medical Record Number: N/A

Admission Date: N/A
Discharge Date: N/A

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for specialized care due to circulatory failure. On admission, he presented with fever, myalgia, headache, and a rash. The patient did not report any ticks or eschar. The patient was initially treated for septic shock with intravenous normal saline. Spotted fever rickettsial infection was considered due to the presence of a rash, and the patient was started on intravenous ceftriaxone and oral doxycycline. As the patient's condition worsened, he developed shortness of breath and hypoxemia, which indicated type 1 respiratory failure. An echocardiogram showed myocarditis and pulmonary edema leading to heart failure. Intravenous chloramphenicol was added to the treatment regimen, as it can be effective in cases like this. Three inotropes were required, including norepinephrine, dobutamine and dopamine, to maintain the patient's blood pressure. After increasing the steroids dosage, the patient began showing signs of improvement. The patient was extubated and transferred back to the High Dependency Unit of the medical ward. The patient was discharged from the hospital ten days following admission.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications:
N/A

Follow-Up:
The patient was reviewed in the out-patient clinic, and he was asymptomatic. Further species identification was not possible due to unavailability of facilities. The patient did not turn up for the follow-up echocardiogram. 

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged in stable condition.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is spotted fever rickettsial infection, which caused septic shock, myocarditis, heart failure and respiratory failure. It was treated with doxycycline and chloramphenicol, and species identification was not possible. It belongs to chapter A (infectious diseases), category A77 (spotted fever).
CODE: A77
